note: Labels written by reading each mutant next to the original, before running review/compare.py.

binary_search/m002.label: bug
binary_search/m002.reason: Search starts at index 1, so a target at index 0 is never found: ([3], 3) gives -1.

count_primes/m006.label: bug
count_primes/m006.reason: For n below 3 it returns None instead of 0.

count_primes/m017.label: bug
count_primes/m017.reason: Index 1 is never cleared, so 1 is counted as a prime: every n >= 3 is one too high.

count_primes/m021.label: bug
count_primes/m021.reason: The sieve loop is gone, so composites are counted: n=10 gives 8, not 4.

count_primes/m025.label: bug
count_primes/m025.reason: Multiples are only crossed off for non-primes, but nothing ever becomes non-prime, so composites stay: n=10 gives 8.

longest_common_prefix/m009.label: bug
longest_common_prefix/m009.reason: Uses the last string as the yardstick & never looks at the first: ['b','a'] gives 'a', not ''.

longest_common_prefix/m017.label: bug
longest_common_prefix/m017.reason: With `and` the early return never fires (or it crashes on a short string): ['ab','ac'] gives 'ab', not 'a'.

lru_cache/m014.label: bug
lru_cache/m014.reason: get() returns 0 instead of the stored value: put(1,10) then get(1) gives 0.

merge_intervals/m024.label: bug
merge_intervals/m024.reason: An overlapping interval no longer extends the end: [[1,3],[2,6]] gives [[1,3]].

merge_intervals/m034.label: bug
merge_intervals/m034.reason: Returns 0 instead of the merged list for any non-empty input.

parse_duration/m023.label: bug
parse_duration/m023.reason: The order check is inverted, so the very first unit is rejected: '45s' raises.

parse_duration/m029.label: bug
parse_duration/m029.reason: next_allowed never advances, so repeats & wrong order are accepted: '1h2h' gives 10800 instead of raising.

parse_duration/m034.label: bug
parse_duration/m034.reason: A trailing number with no unit is silently ignored: '15' gives 0 instead of raising.

rle_encode/m011.label: bug
rle_encode/m011.reason: `count` is never initialised, so any non-empty string crashes when it's first used.

rle_encode/m015.label: bug
rle_encode/m015.reason: The second character is skipped: 'ab' gives 'a'.

rle_encode/m024.label: bug
rle_encode/m024.reason: Subtracting a string from a string raises TypeError as soon as a run ends: 'ab' crashes.

rle_encode/m031.label: bug
rle_encode/m031.reason: Later runs start counting at 2: 'ab' gives 'ab2'.

rle_encode/m038.label: bug
rle_encode/m038.reason: A final run of length 1 gets a count: 'a' gives 'a1'.

roman_to_int/m002.label: bug
roman_to_int/m002.reason: Total starts at 1, so every answer is one too high.

roman_to_int/m006.label: bug
roman_to_int/m006.reason: Nothing is ever added: every numeral gives 0.

roman_to_int/m019.label: bug
roman_to_int/m019.reason: Values are only ever subtracted, never added: 'III' gives 0.

spiral_order/m037.label: bug
spiral_order/m037.reason: The top row of every ring is never read: [[1]] gives [].

spiral_order/m047.label: bug
spiral_order/m047.reason: The right edge never moves in, so cells are read twice: [[1,2],[3,4]] repeats the 4.

spiral_order/m056.label: bug
spiral_order/m056.reason: The bottom row runs one column too far & wraps to index -1: a 2x2 gives [1,2,4,3,4].

spiral_order/m058.label: bug
spiral_order/m058.reason: The bottom row is read in steps of 2, so a 3x3 misses the 7.

spiral_order/m060.label: bug
spiral_order/m060.reason: The bottom row of every ring is never read: a 2x2 misses the 3.

spiral_order/m064.label: bug
spiral_order/m064.reason: The bottom edge never moves up, so cells are read twice: a 2x2 gives [1,2,4,3,3].

top_k_frequent/m011.label: bug
top_k_frequent/m011.reason: The guard is inverted: every positive k returns [].

top_k_frequent/m020.label: bug
top_k_frequent/m020.reason: Returns 0 instead of a list for every positive k.

count_primes/m005.label: equivalent
count_primes/m005.reason: n=2 builds [True, True], clears both & counts 0, the same as returning 0 early.

count_primes/m020.label: equivalent
count_primes/m020.reason: The extra pass with i=1 does nothing because is_prime[1] is already False.

count_primes/m023.label: equivalent
count_primes/m023.reason: The extra pass happens only when i*i == n, & then range(i*i, n, i) is empty.

longest_common_prefix/m013.label: equivalent
longest_common_prefix/m013.reason: Comparing the first string with itself can never find a mismatch.

max_subarray_sum/m019.label: equivalent
max_subarray_sum/m019.reason: When current is exactly 0, `0 + value` & `value` are the same number.

max_subarray_sum/m020.label: equivalent
max_subarray_sum/m020.reason: For integers `current < 1` means `current <= 0` (see m019). With fractions it's a real bug: [0.5, 1] would give 1 instead of 1.5. The task says integers.

max_subarray_sum/m027.label: equivalent
max_subarray_sum/m027.reason: Re-assigning best to an equal value changes nothing.

merge_intervals/m015.label: equivalent
merge_intervals/m015.reason: The first interval is compared with a copy of itself & absorbed. An invalid interval like [5,1] would be duplicated, but the task promises start <= end.

merge_intervals/m026.label: equivalent
merge_intervals/m026.reason: Re-assigning the end to an equal value changes nothing.

parse_duration/m010.label: equivalent
parse_duration/m010.reason: A position is never negative, so `position < -1` & `position < 0` are both always false.

parse_duration/m020.label: equivalent
parse_duration/m020.holds: same result or same error type; the error message differs
parse_duration/m020.reason: Every input the reference rejects still raises ValueError, but from int('') or str.index() with a different message. A test that checked the message text would tell them apart.

spiral_order/m006.label: equivalent
spiral_order/m006.reason: Checks whether the last row is empty instead of the first. Same thing when all rows have equal length; differs for ragged input like [[1], []].

spiral_order/m011.label: equivalent
spiral_order/m011.reason: At that early return `result` is still the empty list.

spiral_order/m025.label: equivalent
spiral_order/m025.reason: Takes the width from the last row instead of the first.

top_k_frequent/m005.label: equivalent
top_k_frequent/m005.reason: Every count is one higher, which doesn't change the ranking. Counts are never returned.

top_k_frequent/m006.label: equivalent
top_k_frequent/m006.reason: Every count is one lower, which doesn't change the ranking.

top_k_frequent/m007.label: equivalent
top_k_frequent/m007.reason: Every count is doubled, which doesn't change the ranking.

top_k_frequent/m012.label: equivalent
top_k_frequent/m012.reason: k=0 falls through to ranked[:0], which is [] anyway.
